# PARITY — five SATUSEHAT SDKs

Identical in the five wikis: `satusehat-integration` (PHP), `-node`, `-python`, `-go`, `-rust`. Every
number is **measured** by `scripts/parity-manifest.sh` (PHP repository) into `SYNC_MANIFEST.json`
schema 3 — never recalled.

## 1. Artefact counts

The table below is **generated** by `scripts/parity-manifest.sh --docs` from `find`/`grep` on each
checkout. Do not edit the numbers: edit the script and re-run it. A hand-copied measurement goes stale
on the next commit, and a stale document is worse than none.

<!-- parity:begin (generated by scripts/parity-manifest.sh --docs, do not edit) -->
Measured: 2026-11-18 · PHP commit `bf5a773`

| section | PHP | Node | Python | Go | Rust |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| payload builder | 141 | 141 | 141 | 141 | 136 |
| datatype | 33 | 33 | 33 | 33 | 12 |
| terminology files | 23 | 23 | 24 | 23 | 1 |
| queue files | 8 | 8 | 8 | 8 | 1 |
| parser files | 142 | 142 | 141 | 142 | 1 |
| test files | 238 | 214 | 220 | 253 | 381 |
| unexported builder methods (Go) | — | — | — | 62 of 1788 | — |

Reading note: the *parser files*, *terminology files*, and *queue files* columns count
**files**, not functions. Rust keeps every parser in one `parser.rs` and terminology in a
single module, so the number is 1 while the functions number in the hundreds. Do not
conclude that Rust covers less from this column — compare through each repository's
`PARITY.md`, which carries the measured function counts.
<!-- parity:end -->

Differences that need explaining, and that will not disappear on their own:

- **Node counts more builder classes than PHP.** Three aliases are included — the canonical name plus
  a legacy name kept so older callers do not break.
- **Go counts one extra parser file** because a helper file matches the `*_parser.go` pattern. The
  per-resource parser count is the same as PHP.
- **Test file counts are not a coverage measure.** One file may hold one test or a hundred; what matters
  is whether both implementations were ever run on the same input — which is what
  `satusehat-conformance` provides.
- **Rust keeps whole layers in one module.** One `parser.rs` holds 133 functions; one `terminology.rs`
  holds the catalog readers. Compare function counts, not module counts.

## 2. Capabilities

| capability | PHP | Node | Python | Go | Rust |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| payload builder | present | present | present | present | present |
| http send | present | present | present | present | present |
| response validation | present | present | present | present | present |
| fhir parser | present | present | present | present | present |
| terminology client | present | present | present | present | present |
| SATUSEHAT required rules | present | present | present | present | present |
| non-standard SATUSEHAT objects | present | present | present | present | present |
| R4 element guard (opt-in) | present | present | gap | present | gap |

`present` means the capability exists in code and has at least one test. Two gaps remain and are not
hidden: Rust has a conformance test but no runtime strict guard, and the guard itself is opt-in
everywhere (`SATUSEHAT_STRICT_R4=1`).

## 3. Measured defects

The unexported methods counted in section 1 belong to the package internals (`set`, `push`, `fail`,
`ref`, `autoPrefix`, `setCodeable`, `dispenseRequest`); no resource setter is hidden. `go build ./...`
is clean and every exported setter is capitalised.

No measured defect is open as of 2026-11-17.

## 4. Naming conventions

| concept | PHP | Node/TS | Python | Go | Rust |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| builder class | `PayloadBuilderPatient` | `Patient` | `PatientBuilder` | `PatientBuilder` | `PatientInput` + `Builder::patient` |
| set one value | `setGender()` | `setGender()` | `set_gender()` | `SetGender()` | struct field `gender` |
| add to a list | `addIdentifier()` | `addIdentifier()` | `add_identifier()` | `AddIdentifier()` | `Vec`/`Option` field |
| result | `->build()` | `.build()` | `.build()` | `.Build()` | `Builder::patient(&input)` |
| validate | `validate()` | `validate()` | `validate()` | `Validate()` | `validate(&value)` |
| send | `SSRequest` | `SSRequest` | `SSRequest` | `SSRequest` | `submit_bundle()` / CLI `push` |
| parser | `PatientParser` | `PatientParser` | `PatientParser` | `PatientParser` | `parser::patient()` |

Two inconsistencies are **deliberate**:

1. **Node names the class after the resource** (`Patient`, not `PatientBuilder`) — TypeScript idiom,
   already a public surface; renaming it would be a breaking change.
2. **Rust uses input structs**, not chained setters — a struct literal forces every required field to
   be supplied; there is no half-built object.

## 5. Equivalent example

```php
$patient = (new PayloadBuilderPatient())->setNik('3201234567890123')
    ->setName('WIWI TJAHJADI')->setGender('female')->setBirthDate('1987-03-14')->build();
```
```ts
const patient = new Patient().setNik('3201234567890123')
  .setName('WIWI TJAHJADI').setGender('female').setBirthDate('1987-03-14').build();
```
```python
patient = (PatientBuilder().set_nik("3201234567890123")
    .set_name("WIWI TJAHJADI").set_gender("female").set_birth_date("1987-03-14").build())
```
```go
patient := builder.NewPatientBuilder().SetNik("3201234567890123").
    SetName("WIWI TJAHJADI").SetGender("female").SetBirthDate("1987-03-14").Build()
```
```rust
let patient = Builder::patient(&PatientInput {
    nik: "3201234567890123".into(), ihs_number: None,
    name: "WIWI TJAHJADI".into(), gender: "female".into(),
    birth_date: "1987-03-14".into(), phone: None, address: None, city: None,
});
```

What is kept equal is the **concept and the JSON produced**, not the call shape. The proof is the
conformance corpus replayed by every port.

## 6. Wiki rule

The same page names exist in all five wikis: `Home`, `Installation`, `Usage`, `Features`,
`PayloadBuilder`, `FHIR-Resources`, `FHIR-DataTypes`, `SSRequest-SSResponse`,
`Validation-Rule-Numbers`, `Error-Handling`, `Onboarding`, `Parity`.

`Parity` must be identical word for word, and it is bilingual: `## English` first, then
`## Bahasa Indonesia`. Check:

```bash
for r in satusehat-integration satusehat-integration-node satusehat-integration-python \
         satusehat-integration-go satusehat-integration-rust; do
  git clone -q https://github.com/ivanwilliammd/$r.wiki.git /tmp/w-$r 2>/dev/null
  sha256sum /tmp/w-$r/Parity.md
done | awk '{print $1}' | sort -u | wc -l     # must be 1
```

## 7. Follow-ups

1. **Rust has no runtime R4 guard.** Its conformance test covers the builder surface, but the opt-in
   strict guard exists only in PHP, Node, Python, and Go.
2. **Wiki and repository copies of this page must be regenerated together**, otherwise the public page
   and the repository disagree.
